data.name: Now Man Flies
data.detailed_description:
In this game you have to explore new lands, flying from one planet to another.
Avoid spaceships, destroy enemies, complete missions and get achievments!

"Sooner or later, our life will have to go beyond this blue-
green ball - or we will die out "- once said Elon Musk, founder
SpaceX. All of us are committed beyond the known, and the most spectacular and unknown
- This space!
Game "Now Man Flies" clearly show what only dreamed and built
the assumption by many generations of researchers. For the "Now Man Flies" - a journey in
the impenetrable darkness of space, almost touch, from planet to planet. it
fierce battle with the ruthless space pirates - for the loser
will remain in the empty space debris iron trash. This meteor shower -
and only the captain's steady hand on the remote control will be able to hold the ship between
meteorites. If you've always wanted to feel like a brave hero,
leading his ship to a distant satellite with an important mission, "Now Man Flies" - is
what do you need!

Control:
←: Turn Left
→: Turn right
space: Use booster

reviews.review:
[h1]Introduction[/h1]
Now Man Flies! Isn’t that a surpise? Well, no since by “now”, you could debate that the first flight of an object heavier than air and still capable of lifting a human being, either occurred during Antiquity in Asia (giant kites) or 18th century France (the Montgolfière hot air balloon). For all his brilliance, Leonardo’s 15th century aerial screw “helicopter” was never a feasible design. Back to our game for now. It’s a casual 2D title which has entertained me enough to overlook its flaws. The second Steam project for developer Epic Fire and the publishing debut for DNB Media.

[h1]Story[/h1]
I can’t really say much for the story since not even a title screen is present, once you boot up the game. From what I could notice however, the “protagonist” can be regarded as a collective character in the form of a space ship which surely needs a crew in order to be maneuvered the way it is. Initially a red rocket which can be switched into a blue one, after 100 planets have been reached. The antagonists are also the obstacles between failure and success in Now Man Flies. Both homing missiles and static satellites will get in the way or even hinder your space exploration efforts.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Even if it might be another Unity-powered title, Now Man Flies fails to mention this and the biggest sin it has commited in my opinion, is the limited Steam Overlay support that it features. Sure, the frame rate counter is present and unsurpringly, it never drops below 60fps even on my native 4K resolution. At least it has Vsync enabled and thus, spares me of having to play at a thousand frames per second. Yes, the graphics aren’t much to look at yet it didn’t bother me one bit. Casual genre is never synonymous with “eye candy”. It’s priced accordingly afterall. Well, in most cases anyway. Now Man Flies won’t allow me to take any screenshots of it through the Overlay and I really can’t understand why some Steam titles still obstruct an innocent feature that can promote the game in question.

[h1]Audio[/h1]
The soundtrack is comprised of just two songs which reminded me of mall elevators. Not repetitive enough to become annoying yet still nothing special. To make matters worse, one song gets unlocked after you pass the aforementioned planet threshold. No voice acting or sound effects are present.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Without any story to begin with, you’d be right in the assessment of the gameplay. It has to compensate the lack of a narrative and in the case of most casual games, that is not an issue. Now Man Flies is not an exception from the rule per se, yet it does become rather repetitive within half an hour, provided you can tolerate its gameplay mechanics for that long. No change of scenery, foes and even controllable ship until you’ve discovered a set number of planets. You might say that the incentive to keep playing is exactly the promise of that new song, ship skin and increased challenge through the unlockable Survival Mode. Reaching it, is only part of the challenge. Now Man Flies has an open-ended structure which means that you can keep on playing for as much as you’d like. And you’ll have to play A LOT until you finally unlock the Steam Achievement for over 32 hours of playtime. To put things into perspective, I’ve seen all that this game has to offer, without even reaching 2 hours of playtime. Good luck dodging the same looking obstacles for another 30! 

You’ll have to endure and even grind through the Classic Mode which has the red rocket travel from planet to planet, all the way to the 100th discovery before the blue vessel takes over. While not a planet for certain, the encounter which makes this transition and marks the culmination of the “campaign”, is a location that resembles the Death Star from Star Wars. What I couldn’t explain was how can so many satellites interfere with space exploration, especially since we’re being led to believe that we’re breaking new grounds with each subsequent discovery. Also, why and who would try to stop these space pioneers through the use of so many guided missiles? If the answer you’re imagining is “aliens”, no other ships or structures are ever encountered. Just the red/blue rocket you’re steering and the far-too-similar-looking blue satellites along with grey projectiles that seem to follow players at an obviously greater velocity than their target.

Monotony is never setting in, simply because you have to become creative, by the time you’ve passed your 50th discovered planet. Beyond the sheer number of obstacles, the randomly generated levels ensure that even if you fail a certain stage repeatedly, you’ll still have to ambition yourself to overcome your mistakes, without having to replay in the same conditions over and over again. Also, the booster mechanic helps plow through foes and reach your destination sooner It can be used as a “I win” button on lower levels. By the time I reached stage 100 though, the booster was only a minor assistance, as instantly covering 10 thousand out of 30 thousand kilometres (only the Metric system is featured in-game) still gave me 20 thousand “reasons” to remain focused on the digital onslaught ahead. Indeed, it was challenging and for this reason alone, I reconsidered my initial intention of slamming this game through a much lower rating.

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
It’s not going to impress you and it certainly won’t keep you as entertained as an excellent RPG or RTS, yet casual games have their very own niche on PCs. We’re not talking of the lazy cash grabs that are prevalent to smartphone “gaming”. Steam needs to host casuals and fortunately, even Now Man Flies is priced within good measure and reason, in perfect balance with its offerings. You get what you pay for, yet it’s still up to you to appreciate the game’s fun factor. Just don’t judge it for its first few levels. If you’re an Achievement collector, it goes without saying that you’ll enjoy this game thoroughly. At the time of this writing, there are five thousand Steam Achievements, waiting to be unlocked within Now Man Flies. With my limited playtime or not, I still managed to gain over three thousand. A considerable number, perhaps even crazy, since I haven’t collected that many in all the Steam games I played in the past combined.

[h1]Strong Points[/h1]
+ Steam Achievements.
+ Adequate scaling of the difficulty factor.
+ Decently priced title offering exactly what it advertises.

[h1]Weak Points[/h1]
- No Steam Trading Cards nor Overlay screenshot support.
- Inherently repetitive gameplay.
- Limited sound selection.

[b]Rating 65/100 [/b]
